correctness.rationale: The Matérn Fourier coefficients obey the explicit power envelope in RESULT.md, and Parseval bounds the squared truncation error on the difference cube by a constant multiple of the squared spectral-coefficient tail for mesh width at most one. The published half-space lemma at transformed smoothness parameter \(2\nu+d/2\) yields the claimed exponent; boundedness of the difference-density produces the all-density mean-square estimate. The exact matrix diagonal correction comes from entry counting. A bounded-differences inequality with per-sample influence \(2M^2/N\) proves finite-sample concentration and the almost-sure limit. The fixed-parameter scope, aliasing conditions and range boundaries were checked. The included supplementary checker passed 171 finite assertions; no finite computation is claimed as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The target source arXiv:2305.11065v1 Section 4 explicitly states the bounded-density iid Matérn Frobenius exponent as Conjecture 9, with a heuristic involving Fourier autocorrelation and no proof. The present claim proves that exponent for all bounded densities using one-period Parseval and gives a finite-sample concentration inequality. arXiv:2210.10210v2 describes the same numerical method and only a heuristic RMS grid rule, not this theorem. Searches for later solutions and analogous formulations did not yield a decisive stronger source; this is evidence for originality, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The explicitly stated Matérn covariance-matrix Conjecture 9 concerns a real numerical rank-selection bottleneck in equispaced Fourier Gaussian process regression. The present bound proves the previously heuristic stronger cutoff exponent \(2\nu+d/2\) for all bounded densities with an explicit constant. The localization and finite-sample diagonal/concentration control identify the validity of the statistical gain rather than merely rephrasing a uniform kernel bound. No extension to arbitrary site laws, moving-parameter arrays or a sharp constant is asserted.
